results.title: Georgia Ports Authority weathers year of tariffs with strong performance
results.content:
GPA moved 5.7 million twenty-foot equivalent container units of cargo in 2025, a 2.6% increase over the previous year, the authority reported Tuesday. GPA leaders cited customers diverting cargo from West Coast ports to the East Coast, and months of shippers “front loading” cargo as contributing to the strong volume. [...] Compared to 2024, GPA saw a 7.5% decline in 2025 volume at the Port of Brunswick, its Roll-On/Roll-Off port for autos and heavy machinery. The drop in volume was driven by tariffs that led to some manufacturers pausing shipments and a decline in exports to China, according to GPA. [...] The OOCL Iris motors toward the Talmadge Bridge as it heads to the Georgia Ports Authority Garden City Terminal on Tuesday, Feb. 25, 2025. The Iris is the largest containership by TEU to ever call on the Port of Savannah.

But the year was not all smooth sailing.

results.title: GARY WISENBAKER: Georgia ports weather tariff turbulence | Valdosta Daily Times
results.content:
Savannah rides a tariff-fueled surge while Brunswick’s auto trade hits the brakes. The Georgia Ports Authority is doing what it does best: moving cargo, even as President Donald Trump’s second term tariff storm rolls across the global trade horizon. The Port of Savannah’s container docks are humming, while Brunswick’s auto terminals are taking a hit. It’s a tale of two ports, one booming, one bracing. [...] This is what tariffs look like on the ground. Manufacturers are holding back shipments from Europe, Asia, and Mexico as costs rise and markets shift. Brunswick’s total auto volume for FY2025 slipped 2.2%, and GPA chief Griff Lynch blamed the downturn squarely on auto-import tariffs.

So while container cargo is coasting on a tariff tailwind, the roll-on/roll-off side is squarely in the headwind. [...] — Tariff clarity — If the White House backs off or trade deals stabilize, shipping may return to a steady, not sprinting, pace.

— Port competition — Savannah’s efficiency could attract even more business as shippers consolidate at high-performance gateways.

— Auto rebound — Brunswick’s fortunes depend on where automakers choose to build and ship next year.

— Infrastructure payoff — GPA’s investment bet needs to keep paying off in speed and reliability.
